Context API: Context API provides a built-in way to share values across the component tree without prop drilling. It's best suited for low-frequency updates like theme, locale, or auth state.
Redux: Redux is a predictable state container with a single store, immutable updates via pure reducers, and actions dispatched to trigger state changes. The Redux Toolkit simplifies boilerplate significantly.
Zustand: Zustand is a minimal state management library with a hook-based API, no boilerplate, and support for middleware. It's ideal for projects that need simple global state without Redux overhead.

Code Splitting: Code splitting breaks your bundle into smaller chunks loaded on demand, reducing initial load time. React.lazy and Suspense make code splitting declarative and easy to implement.

Lazy Loading: Lazy loading defers loading of non-critical resources until they are needed. Combined with Suspense, it shows a fallback UI while the lazy component loads asynchronously.
Memoization: React.memo is a higher-order component that prevents re-rendering when props haven't changed. useCallback memorizes callback functions to maintain referential equality across renders.

JSX: JSX is a syntax extension for JavaScript that looks like HTML and allows you to write markup inside your components. It gets transpiled to React.createElement calls under the hood by tools like Babel.
Components: Components are reusable, self-contained pieces of UI that can be either function-based or class-based. Modern React favors functional components with hooks.
Props: Props (short for properties) are read-only inputs passed to components from their parent. They enable parent-to-child communication and make components configurable.

useState: useState is a hook that adds local state to function components. It returns a stateful value and a function to update it, triggering a re-render when called.
useEffect: useEffect lets you perform side effects in function components such as data fetching, subscriptions, or DOM manipulation. The dependency array controls when the effect re-runs.
useRef: useRef returns a mutable ref object whose .current property persists across renders without causing re-renders. It's commonly used to access DOM elements directly.

useContext: useContext consumes a context value created by React.createContext, allowing deep prop drilling to be avoided. It re-renders the component when the context value changes.
useReducer: useReducer is an alternative to useState for complex state logic involving multiple sub-values or when the next state depends on the previous one. It follows the reducer pattern from Redux.
useMemo: useMemo memoizes the result of an expensive computation, recomputing only when its dependencies change. Use it to optimize performance by avoiding unnecessary recalculations.

CSS Modules: CSS Modules scope CSS class names locally by default, preventing naming collisions across components. Files are imported like JavaScript objects and class names are accessed as properties.
Styled Components: Styled Components is a CSS-in-JS library that lets you write actual CSS inside your JavaScript using tagged template literals. It automatically handles vendor prefixing and scoping.
Tailwind: Tailwind CSS is a utility-first framework providing low-level classes for rapid UI building. It pairs well with React through class composition and tools like clsx for conditional classes.

Controlled Forms: In controlled forms, form elements derive their value from React state and update via onChange handlers. This gives React single source of truth for form data and enables validation.
React Router: React Router is the standard routing library for React apps, enabling navigation between views while keeping the UI in sync with the URL. It supports nested routes, params, and lazy loading.

Jest: Jest is a delightful JavaScript testing framework with zero configuration, built-in assertions, mocking, and code coverage. It's the default test runner in Create React App.
React Testing Library: React Testing Library builds on top of DOM Testing Library and encourages testing components from the user's perspective. It queries rendered output rather than testing implementation details.
Cypress: Cypress is an end-to-end testing framework that runs in the browser, providing real-time reloads, time travel debugging, and automatic waiting. It's ideal for integration and E2E tests.

useTransition: useTransition marks state updates as non-urgent transitions, keeping the UI responsive during expensive re-renders. The isPending flag shows a loading state without blocking user input.
useDeferredValue: useDeferredValue lets you defer re-rendering a non-urgent part of the tree. The deferred value lags behind the real value, allowing urgent updates (like input typing) to stay responsive.

RSC Basics: React Server Components run exclusively on the server, never sent to the client. They reduce bundle size by keeping heavy dependencies server-side and can directly access databases and file systems.
Server Actions: Server Actions are async functions that run on the server, invoked from client components. Use 'use server' to mark them, enabling direct mutations without building API routes.

Error Boundaries: Error Boundaries catch JavaScript errors in their child component tree, displaying a fallback UI instead of crashing the whole app. Class components with componentDidCatch are required.
Error Recovery: Use key props to reset error boundaries. Changing the key unmounts and remounts the component tree, clearing the error state without a full page refresh.

Portals: Portals render children into a DOM node outside the parent component's hierarchy, useful for modals, tooltips, and dropdowns that need to escape overflow or z-index clipping.
TypeScript with React: TypeScript with React provides type safety for props, state, hooks, and event handlers. Use generic types for useState, useRef, and forwardRef for stricter typing.

React Server Components (RSC): React Server Components render on the server, reducing client bundle size by sending only the rendered output. RSC can directly access databases, files, and backend services without exposing secrets to the client. 'use client' directive marks client components. Server components cannot use hooks, event handlers, or browser APIs. App Router (Next.js 13+) uses RSC by default. Benefits: direct backend access, zero client JS for static content, automatic code splitting, and streaming HTML. Streaming with Suspense sends UI progressively as data loads, improving perceived performance.
React Hooks Advanced: Advanced React hooks for complex state management: useReducer for state with complex transitions (like Redux without the boilerplate). useCallback memoizes functions to prevent child re-renders. useMemo memoizes expensive computations. useRef stores mutable values across renders without causing re-renders. useLayoutEffect runs synchronously after DOM mutations. useTransition marks state updates as non-urgent. useDeferredValue debounces rapidly-changing values. Custom hooks compose these primitives. The React Compiler (React Forget) automatically memoizes values, making explicit memoization optional.
